task: detect maize lodging in field plots from UAV image features
note: SMOTE-ENN applied after the 70:30 split but to training and test sets separately (Table 5); tuning CV apparently on resampled training set. Before/after comparison uses different test sets. Tabular features extracted from UAV images.

task: detect DDoS attacks in IoT network traffic
note: Four boosting models x SMOTE/Borderline-SMOTE on CICDDoS2019 and KDDCUP99; no unresampled baseline. F1 named in abstract but absent from result tables; MAE, RMSE, training time coded other.

task: segment satellite images into village, mountain and river areas
note: Unsupervised FCM/possibilistic clustering on pixel intensities of two satellite images; resampling uses ground-truth labels; no split or CV, evaluated on the same images' original pixels. Compares ROS, RUS, SMOTE within the application.

task: detect noble-gas-instability fault precursors in vacuum ion pump pressure data
note: SMOTE (50% ratio) combined with cost-sensitive SVM vs cost-sensitive SVM alone; CNN cost-sensitive only. Four splits incl. cross-pump and temporal. 'Post-deployment' evaluation looks like retrospective run on 54 new pumps 2022-2025, so validation coded external.

task: distinguish treatment-induced effects from recurrent glioblastoma in MRI tissue-sample patches
note: Full text is the meeting abstract itself (Neuro-Oncology suppl. p. vii177), identical to record abstract. Oversampling method not named; read as plain oversampling of TxE samples. Test set is one third of patients withheld, same cohort.

task: classify low-grade glioma molecular subtypes (IDH, 1p/19q) from MRI radiomics
note: Radiomics features from MRI (tabular). Authors call the 42-patient test set external, but both parts are drawn from the same TCGA-LGG cohort (four sites), so validation coded internal. No unresampled baseline.

task: predict vector-borne diseases such as dengue and malaria from symptom records
note: Text inconsistent: abstract claims environmental/clinical data and precision/recall/F1, but data are a public 41-class symptom dataset and only accuracy is reported; K-Means used as classifier; mentions lung cancer. Abstract says 'oversampling'; text names SMOTE and undersampling.

task: classify stress level (low, moderate, high) from physiological and lifestyle data
note: Two datasets (hospital IT staff sensor data; UCI/Kaggle lifestyle survey), each split 80:20. Precision/recall/F1/AUC named but only accuracy reported. 'No sampling' baseline mentioned qualitatively only, confounded with PSS relabelling.
